title: Monitoring the Reductive and Oxidative Half-Reactions of a Flavin-Dependent Monooxygenase using Stopped-Flow Spectrophotometry
protocol: Prepare 1 L of 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer at pH 7.5.
Pour 250 mL of the buffer into a 500-mL Büchner flask containing a stir bar.
Seal the flask with a rubber stopper and place it on a stir plate.
Connect the short tube of the flask to a Schlenk line.
Degas the buffer under vacuum for 5 hours at room temperature with agitation.
Perform 5 consecutive rounds of vacuum degassing and flushing with argon every hour.
Flush the flask with argon for 10 seconds and disconnect it from the vacuum manifold.
Place the flask inside the glove box.
Leave the flask open in the glove box overnight with vigorous agitation.
Prepare 1 L of 0.1 M sodium acetate at pH 5.0.
Pour 125 mL of this buffer into a 250-mL Büchner flask and perform steps 1.2-1.4.
Weigh out 5 mg glucose oxidase from Aspergillus niger (181300 U/g) in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Weigh out 0.9 g glucose using a 50 mL Falcon conical tube.
Place both containers into the glove box.
Dissolve glucose oxidase and glucose in 50 mL of anaerobic 0.1 M sodium acetate, pH 5.0 (final concentrations of 18.13 U/mL and 100 mM, respectively).
Fill the reservoir syringes with this solution.
Ensure that the drive valves are in the "load" position.
Fill the drive syringes.
Turn the F valve to the "drive" position.
Empty the stop syringe by clicking on Empty in the Pro-Data control software.
Push the buffer from drive syringe F through the flow circuit by manually raising the corresponding drive ram.
Repeat this step ten times in total.
Perform the same procedure with the other three drive syringes.
Wait one hour.
Replace the solution of the reservoir syringes with the same buffer containing glucose oxidase and glucose.
Push the new buffer from the drive syringe through the flow circuit by manually raising the corresponding drive ram, repeating this step ten times in total.
Perform the same procedure with the other three drive syringes.
Allow the solution to stand in the flow system overnight.
After overnight incubation, repeat step 2.5 (pushing the buffer from the drive syringe through the flow circuit by manually raising the corresponding drive ram).
Prepare 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.5) and pour 50 mL into a 50-mL vial with a stir bar.
Cap the vial with a Wheaton stopper and a Wheaton aluminum seal.
Place the vial on ice.
Immerse a long needle connected to a tank containing 100% oxygen into the solution.
Insert another short needle through the stopper of the vial as a vent.
Bubble the solution with 100% oxygen for 1 hour with agitation.
First remove the short needle from the vial and wait 10 seconds before removing the long needle.
Place the closed vial in the glove box.
Weigh out 1 mg of NADPH in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Place the Eppendorf tube into the glove box.
Dissolve NADPH in 300 μL of anaerobic 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.5.
Remove 30 μL from the solution to determine NADPH concentration with a spectrophotometer (ε340 nm= 6,270 M-1cm-1).
Take 400 μL of enzyme stock solution from the freezer and thaw in the glove box.
Transfer the enzyme solution into a 25-mL vial with a stir bar.
Cap the vial with a Wheaton stopper and aluminum seal.
Place the vial on ice and connect it to a Schlenk line by inserting a needle through the stopper.
Perform 5 consecutive rounds of vacuum degassing and flushing with argon every 20 minutes for 1 hour.
Flush the vial with argon for 10 seconds and disconnect from the vacuum manifold.
Place the vial on ice inside the glove box.
Prepare the stopped-flow instrument and Pro-Data control software for single mixing mode following the manufacturer's protocol.
Turn on a circulating water bath (15 °C).
Bubble nitrogen through the water to remove oxygen for 20 minutes.
Maintain the temperature of the drive syringes and the observation cell at 15 °C.
Select Photodiode Array, External trigger, and Logarithmic scale in the Control Panel window.
Launch the Pro-Data viewer software.
Define the directory for storing data files.
Replace the solution of reservoir syringes C and F with anaerobic 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.5).
Turn the C and F valves to the "drive" position.
Empty the stop syringe by clicking Empty in the Pro-Data control software.
Push the buffer from both drive syringes through the flow circuit five times manually.
Perform step 6.6 four times in total to ensure complete removal of glucose oxidase from the flow circuit.
Click on Baseline in the Pro-Data control software.
Mix 100 μL of enzyme stock solution with 1100 μL of anaerobic 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer (final concentration after mixing in the stopped flow of 15 μM).
Replace the solution in reservoir syringe F with the enzyme solution.
Turn the F valve to the "drive" position.
Empty the stop syringe by clicking Empty in the Pro-Data control software.
Push the enzyme solution from drive syringe F through the flow circuit manually three times.
Set the acquisition time to 60 s in the Pro-Data control software.
Ensure both drive syringes are filled with their corresponding solutions and rams contact pistons.
Turn both valves to the "drive" position and click Acquire to perform the drive.
Repeat step to obtain data in triplicate.
Determine enzyme concentration before mixing using A452 nm value (ε452 nm = 13,700 M-1cm-1).
Prepare 4 mL of NADPH solution 1.5-fold more concentrated than required.
Replace the solution in reservoir syringe C with the NADPH solution.
Empty and refill the stop syringe three times as described.
Repeat step to obtain reduction spectra.
Prepare stopped-flow instrument and Pro-Data control software for double mixing mode following manufacturer's protocol.
Repeat steps 6.2-6.5.
Replace the solution in the four reservoir syringes with anaerobic 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.5).
Turn the F valve to the "drive" position.
Empty the stop syringe by clicking Empty in the Pro-Data control software.
Push the buffer from the drive syringe F through the flow circuit by manually raising the corresponding drive ram.
Perform this step five times in total with each drive syringe.
Perform step 7.3 four times in total to completely remove the contents from the flow circuit.
Click Baseline in the Pro-Data control software.
Mix 200 μL of enzyme stock solution with 1000 μL of anaerobic 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer (final concentration after mixing in the stopped flow of 15 μM).
Replace the solution of reservoir syringe A with the enzyme solution.
Turn the A valve to the "drive" position.
Empty the stop syringe by clicking Empty in the Pro-Data control software.
Push the enzyme solution from drive syringe A through the flow circuit by manually raising the corresponding drive ram.
Perform this step three times in total.
In the Pro-Data control software, set the delay time to 0.5 s and acquisition time to 60 s.
Ensure that all drive syringes are filled with their corresponding solutions.
Position the drive rams in contact with the drive syringe pistons.
Turn all valves to the "drive" position.
Click Acquire in the Pro-Data control software to perform the drive.
Repeat step 7.8 two more times to obtain data in triplicate.
Replace the solution of reservoir syringe B with an NADPH solution 1.5-fold more concentrated than the enzyme solution in syringe A.
Turn the B valve to the "drive" position.
Empty and refill the stop syringe three times as described in 7.7.
Replace the solution of reservoir syringe C with oxygenated buffer.
Turn the C valve to the "drive" position.
Empty and refill the stop syringe three times as described in 7.7.
Set the delay and acquisition time at 15 and 900 seconds, respectively, in Pro-Data control software.
Repeat step 7.8.
Launch the Pro-Data converter software.
Click on the Options icon and select Save in ProDataCSV.
Open the directory where the data files were stored.
Drag the files to the APL Pro-Data converter window.
The data will be saved automatically as CSV format files in the same directory.
Open the CSV format files using Microsoft Excel.
Normalize the baseline of the stopped-flow traces by subtracting the corresponding absorption at 700 nm.
Analyze the corrected traces using KaleidaGraph.
Fit the plot of absorbance at the corresponding maximum versus time to an appropriate exponential function.
Plot the absorbance at 452 nm as a function of time.
Use a double exponential equation for data fitting.
Calculate rates of 0.65 and 0.23 s-1 for the first and second phase of flavin reduction, respectively.
Analyze stopped-flow traces at 380 and 452 nm to determine intermediate formation and reoxidation rates.
Use a single exponential equation for data fitting.
Calculate rates of 1.4 and 0.006 s-1 for the first and second step of the oxidative half-reaction, respectively.
